fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Perimeter Fencing; Water Feature; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Water Feature; Limited Rear Access; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance that is visible from both directions of travel on the street.

• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the residence without obstruction.

• Mark any gate or fence entry points with reflective indicators so responders can locate access points quickly at night or in low-visibility conditions.

• Keep at least one gate in the perimeter fencing unlocked or fitted with a breakaway lock to allow responders to reach the rear of the property on foot.

• Trim any vegetation along the driveway that reduces vertical or side clearance for emergency vehicles.

• Clear a level area near the residence where an ambulance or fire apparatus can stop and turn around, even if it requires repositioning stored items or vehicles during an emergency.

• Mark the water feature with a visible indicator so responders moving on foot at night are aware of its location and can avoid it.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Vegetation Along Driveway; Mixed Vegetation; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from trees growing closest to the structure where vegetation is touching or within a few feet of the roofline or walls.

• Thin the tree cluster nearest the structure to create open space between individual trees and between the trees and the building.

• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.

• Clear low-hanging branches from large trees near the structure so fire cannot climb from ground level into the tree canopy.

• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches that could block vehicle access or drop burning material onto vehicles during an evacuation.

• Thin vegetation growing along both sides of the driveway to maintain a clear travel path and improve visibility along the route.

• Maintain the single access route free of debris, fallen branches, and encroaching vegetation at all times, as it is the only way in and out for residents and responders.
